utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this way of proceedings because there are a number of houses here. They have suffered -- some of them, it appears, very -- whole damage, or varying degrees of damage. If this witness is going to give any helpful evidence about what happened, he would need to say, well this house, this bit of damage was or wasn't there on a certain date, this other bit was -- these houses as we know have been reconstructed. In the meantime these photographs were taken years later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right I take it over. Witness, you have identified a number of houses all of which at first glance appear to have suffered some kind of damage; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you tell us approximately when that damage was caused to these houses, whether they were all damaged more or less at the same time on the same occasion or whether they were damaged on different occasions for different or various reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we reckon that they were damaged, all of them, on the 7th of January, and while they were holding this line, they removed the joinery or burnt what was not burnt once then realised that we had to -- that they had to withdraw. Maybe it had -- didn't happen on the same day because we stayed there for -- they stayed there for a certain period of time. It doesn't mean that it was all done on the same day as it looks in the pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it also possible that some of them --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- that some of the houses you identified may have been damaged on the occasion of the 8th of August or not, 8th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes Madam Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour. I just have two additional questions, and then I'll end my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic did you receive compensation for any of the items taken from your home from any one?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. In 1994, or 1995, I was given some 5.000 German marks which was not enough to cover even the window frames as you could see from the picture that the house was damaged, and I received only 5.000 German marks. Some people received donations and mended their house with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This, registrar, this photo over here, has it been tendered or not? Are you tendering this photo or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you haven't asked the witness any question on this photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just have the usher's assistance for one second and we can get this completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, I'd ask you to take a look at the photograph being shown to you. That is ERN 01087863. And ask you if you recognise what's in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you know, you know. If you don't know, you don't know, but we cannot waste time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I will complete at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But do you want to tender it into evidence or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We'll leave it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Madam Vidovic. You can take that photo away. He's finished with it. And -- Mr. Rankovic, you're now going to be asked a series of questions by Madam Vidovic who is appearing for the defendant. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Rankovic.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the usher please put Prosecution Exhibits P394, that's the map that we have seen today and shown to the witness, and I suppose it will be helpful to the witness to answer the questions that I'm going to ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, you said that you were born in the Bratunac municipality and that you spent the whole of your life in Bratunac municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, up to this date. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you said that the defence in your village was established in mid-April. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't established. We organised that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You organised that.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said in response to the Prosecutor's question about the situation prevailing at the beginning of the war, that is in April and May and the following months that preceded the attack that we are discussing now, that is the attack of the 8th of August, you described the situation as being unpleasant in the area.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, definitely it was unpleasant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's question, you said that the defence of your village undertook no action in the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No action was taken. We remained in our villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show on the map again where your village of Jezestica is and where the village of Glogova is.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the village of Jezestica and this is Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that it is in close proximity, that Glogova is very near to your village?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again. May I appeal again to you, Madam Vidovic and to the witness in particular, since you speak the same --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- since you speak the same language and whatever you're saying needs to be translated to us, please allow an interval of time between question and answer so that the interpreters in the meantime can catch up with you and translate to us. Because otherwise, if one jumps over the other immediately without an interval we will miss a part of the testimony. In fact, at the moment, for example, they did not catch up with you. They don't know what you replied to the previous question or to the last question that Madam Vidovic put to you. And the question was -- you're looking at something different here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer my question?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that it is in close proximity, that Glogova is very near to your village.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, between my house and the entrance of Glogova across the village and Magasici it will take about one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately up to four kilometres to the centre of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, is it possible that you didn't notice any happenings in the village of Glogova in April and May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I personally didn't. I am telling you only what I know, but what I don't know I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was happening with the Muslim population of Magasici village? There were Muslims there at the time as well.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, did you pass through that area in the period between May and August 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I passed in 1992. I went for a celebration of Djurdjev Dan, and later I went to my house, and I passed through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you notice burnt houses in Glogova and the burnt mosque?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I passed down the roundabout way. I didn't have any need to go through Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Rankovic, let us move on. When exactly the conflict in Bratunac break out?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when the conflict in Bratunac broke out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that Bratunac was a mixed community. Isn't it true that the area of Bratunac before the war had more than 21.000 Muslims and about eleven and a half thousand Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, when I was young, I worked on the ground, and I stayed in my village until 1980, and then I opened my own store. As I -- and I was not interested in Bratunac because I went to work in Belgrade. So I know very little about Bratunac and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the beginning of the war in Bratunac in 1992. Do you know perhaps what happened to the Muslims of Bratunac in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about any happenings, any events, any killings in the elementary school called Vuk Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did and I didn't. I don't know. I'm going to tell you today only what I know. What I don't know, I cannot speak about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you exactly hear?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot the say. I cannot tell you anything off the top of my head and I cannot invent things that I never saw. What I testify of testify to is what I've seen with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but during your testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but when you testified about this, you were not testifying about things that you knew. In fact, you even described it as "there were rumours." So you did testify on rumours. So you need to decide whether you're going to testify on facts that you know about only and leave out rumours completely or not, but you personally came here to The Hague with this document in hand, which you handed to the Prosecution and testified about it, even though you described it as a rumour. This is why in the beginning I told you you cannot distinguish or discriminate between the Prosecution or the Defence. Your duty is to answer truthfully and fully each and every question which is put to you irrespective of who is putting the question to you. Let's proceed now, Ms. -- Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It was exactly what I wanted to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony, you heard about -- you testified about what you heard. What did you hear about the events in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, I heard that the Muslims were expelled there on the 2nd of August, and that's what I omitted to say before. A relative of mine, Milisav went --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, could you please answer to my questions, but we'll come to that later. Therefore, you said that the Muslim population were expelled from Bratunac. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, isn't it true that the defence of the area of Kravica, including your village, was organised months before, maybe even the whole year before with respect to the time that you mentioned in your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, are you saying that you did not take active part in organising the defence?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, you were not even an ordinary citizen of Jezestica. You were a member of the local board of the SDS, which was under the Bratunac Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the SDS, but this is unrelated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please speak slowly so the Judges can hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question. Therefore, you were an SDS member of Jezestica which was under the Bratunac Serbian Democratic Party branch? You were not an ordinary citizen. Therefore, you were involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you were a member of the SDS local board of the Jezestica that was part of the Bratunac Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you join the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now kindly ask the usher to put on the ELMO documents number 00835830, and I would like to note at the same time to the Trial Chamber and to the Prosecution that the English translation has the mark L0041625, and it refers to the extract from the SDS list of the Bratunac 1990 list of membership.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, could you please look at page 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't -- we don't have this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tell you now the page number it's 008358 -- [In English] Okay. Only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be D29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: D29. Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness to look at page 00835830 and number 484 on that page. If the usher could push the page up a little bit so we can see number 484. Mr. Rankovic, do you see this now?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you joined the Serbian Democratic Party on the 26th of August, 1990?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I don't know the date, but I did join, yes. I can't remember the exact date, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Is it correct that you remained a member of the SDS throughout the year 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nobody ever invited me to go there, nor did I go, nor am I a member of any party now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that you were not a member of the SDS during 1991?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly that you were not a member?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: As I say, I admit that I was a member. I don't know what the years were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any need for me to show you evidence that you were a member of the party, the SDA party, in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I accept that. I was a member. I'm not any more. But nobody ever contacted me about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We are satisfied with the response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps he can tell us -- just a moment. Perhaps he can tell us when he stopped paying the membership fee. Do you recall when you stopped paying the membership fee to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I paid a membership fee only once, on only one occasion. After that, I never went there any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that in 1991 you did not pay your membership fees?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: As I'm telling you, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let's move on, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it's correct that you joined the SDA [as interpreted] very early on, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was no audible reply from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, one moment, because the transcript says SDA. That should be the SDS. That's to start with. And I think you can skip this question -- forward, Madam Vidovic, because if he joined in 1990, then the answer is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I did not understand whether the document I tendered has received a number. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It is D29.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, members of the SDS received instructions for their work from the SDS leadership, did they not?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you were a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, but there was a narrow circle. It wasn't me or my children in the house who knew. As I said, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher please put on the ELMO document number 00349515.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document of the president of the S [as interpreted], Dr. Radovan Karadzic, of the 15th of August, 1991. It's "Entitled Operating Instructions Obligatory For Everybody". Witness, please look at item four of this document which reads: "Every member of a local board must be entrusted with maintaining contact with ten to 20 households." Mr. Rankovic, as a member of the SDS you certainly knew about this instruction.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not -- no, no. I didn't. I certainly didn't know about it, because I was not active as a member. I had family problems, so I was more concerned about my family problems than about the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that you yourself were not an active member of the SDS and that you did not go to SDS meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could this document that has been shown to the witness be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it will be D30, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, is it correct that apart from you, the SDS had another 25 members in your village of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that you just went there, signed up, and then you knew nothing further about it?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: All I know about myself is, well, perhaps when the first meeting was held. After that, I didn't attend any more meetings. And I can only speak for myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps that Mr. Miladin Bogdanovic was also a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the SDS was very active in Bratunac, including your area?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I say, I'm not a politician. I didn't go to any meetings in Bratunac. I wasn't all that interested in politics. And I'm speaking now about myself, about me personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, the SDS was moreover preparing defence lines and units for war in the area in 1991. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never heard about that?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will only mention that we ask the Chamber to take notice of the judgement in the Deronjic case. I will now read two brief parts of the interview given by Mr. Deronjic to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 23rd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. This is not the way to do it. Could the usher please escort the witness out of the courtroom for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I had to stop you because the way to do it is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. precisely along the lines that was raised by yourselves earlier on. The practice is or shouldn't be or it's not desirable that you tell the witness who said whatever you're going to put to him. You select whatever you want to put to the witness without telling him who said that. You just put to the witness, "What do you have to state as regards the following statement," or, "Would you agree with the following statement," but you don't tell the witness who has made that statement or on what occasions, et cetera. Now, unfortunately, he has already heard the name of the person that -- so I would suggest to you that you skip this part and come to it later on and you move along with some other questions. At least we'll try to save what we could save, because otherwise I would -- I would have to tell you no, you cannot put this question. I'm going to allow it, but after some time. First you proceed with other questions. When you come to it, you tell the witness, "If I were to suggest to you that this is what happened on such-and-such and day and such-and-such a place, would you agree or not?" But you don't tell him, "This has been stated to us by Mr. Deronjic," or whoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may in addition, I would object to the Court having to take judicial notice of it, if that's where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am not taking -- we are not taking judicial notice. This is why I'm saying you put to the witness this statement and then ask the witness whether he agrees with that statement. It doesn't mean -- it's not tantamount to --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- taking judicial notice. I mean... And obviously, if there is not going to ever be agreement on the part of the Prosecution re: the suggested matters from the Deronjic case to be taken as judicial notice of -- and then obviously we are not going to. It's as simple as that. Yes. Let's bring the witness in. I think -- have you understood?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I have understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's bring the witness in again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rankovic, let me explain very briefly. We had to send you out of the courtroom. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We had to send you out of the courtroom for a while because we had to rectify something. Madam Vidovic was going to read out to you an extract from a statement by Mr. Deronjic. That cannot be done, so we will move to the next question. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, as a member of the SDS, you are aware of the fact that the SDS organised Crisis Staffs, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not. If they did something in Bratunac and Kravica, I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything at all about the Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I was in my village the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Crisis Staffs organised lines of defence?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I told you where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to say that there were three small Serb areas or small regions in the Bratunac area, including Kravica, and that in 1991 detachments were organised there, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, nor do I know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would now ask the usher to put on the ELMO Defence document D4. D4. Which is an order on mobilisation in the Serbian municipality of Bratunac issued by the Crisis Staff on the 16th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, please take a look at this document. Is it not correct that this document a purpose to declare a state of emergency for all citizens in the Bratunac municipality as of the 16th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but as I said in mid-April we had the village guards. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does the holding of this guard, the beginning of the guard, have any connection with the date of this mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I said it happened in mid-April. That's when we started holding the guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, do you agree that Jezestica is a village belonging to the Kravica commune and that belongs to Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now put on the ELMO document 01320274. 013202747, which is a decision of the government of the Serbian municipality of Bratunac on the payment of remuneration to members of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality and others for May 1992, and BiH Serb army units in the area of Bratunac. And the date is the 25th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please let me finish my question. Would you please look at the first part of this decision. I quote: "This decision determines the remuneration for May 1992 for members of the Serb army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is the battalion in Bratunac, members of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality..." So behind the comma it says, "Members of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality." And then also before replying, please look at part II, that says, "Members, that is persons attending the training at the army camp in Skelani and volunteers shall be paid remuneration for May in the amount of 50.000 dinars in cash, and 17 persons in the Skelani camp also have the right, they're entitled to remuneration amounting to 20.000 dinars in coupons." My question, sir: Is it correct that there was a military camp in Skelani for training in May 1992? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I have visited Skelani only twice in my 50 years. I've only passed through once in 1970. I don't know anything about Skelani. Either Skelani --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In respect to this, I'll rephrase my question. Is it true, Mr. Rankovic, that the volunteers from Serbia had been paid to fight in the area of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that you, as someone who was a member of the SDS, could have ignored to such an extent what had been happening in your municipality, to be unaware totally of anything that was happening around you in Bratunac, even in the village of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Just as I don't know now because I work in the field and I go home twice a month and then I go back to work, maybe the same happened at the time. All those major members who were involved knew about that but I wasn't such a member and I don't know about things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I proceed with my next question, can this please -- this document be tendered as a Defence exhibit, and the number is 013202747.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and this will be Defence Exhibit D31.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, you said that apart from the tension and unease that you felt in Jezestica before August 1992, it was peaceful.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put on the ELMO document number 01 -- so document 01321099, dated 29th September, 1993. That's the document issued by the Bratunac military post, seized by the Prosecution, and it is part of the financial package of documents seized by the Prosecution, and it is entitled "Record Sheet For A Dead Combatant".

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic could you please look at this record sheet and it's content. It's clear this refers to Mihajlo Uzelac, a volunteer from Zemun who was killed in combat operation on the 29th of June 1992 in Jezestica. Now, in connection with this, my question is: Mr. Rankovic, Zemun is a town in Belgrade near Serbia, isn't?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I said that Jezestica is a large area. It stretches all the way to Magasici. Whether he was there and my hamlet Rankovici, I didn't see him there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, why the volunteers from Serbia were getting killed in June 1992 if there was peace at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I told you, I don't know. I cannot say whether he was killed or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean that you knew nothing that volunteers from Serbia were getting killed in your village?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not in my village. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Be given a number and the document number is 01321099.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document can become Defence Exhibit D32.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic you yourself just told us about an incident that occurred on the 2nd of August 1992 which involved your relatives Ljubomir Rankovic and Milislav Rankovic who were wounded in Jezestica -- in Glogova on the 2nd of August, 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were they doing in Glogova at the time? Those were your relatives from Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. They went from our village Rankovici. They drove their wife -- wife to the doctor, to Glogova. There was a barricade on the road, and the Lada car skidded off the road because there were shots coming from the water. Both men were wounded. They ran away, and the woman remained in the car and the car was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the usher please put on the ELMO document number D22, Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D22.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness please look at page 02887. Mr. Rankovic, what actually happened in Glogova on the 2nd of August, 1992? Could you please look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. When are we getting this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This D22 document. I'll wait for a while before I ask my question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Witness, you have looked at this document, I hope. Can you look at the names under numbers 2, 9, 24, 31, 36, and 46 -- 43 on this list. Do you wish to say that they were just passing by and driving through Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I know nothing about this. I am familiar with five people from this list at the most.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that these two relatives of yours are on this list?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Glogova is a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this took place precisely a few days before the attack on your village?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let me ask you another question. You said that you are originally from the village of Rankovici, which is a hamlet, in fact, of Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this. Are you aware that precisely in the section of your small village of Rankovici artillery weapons were deployed, for example, a gun?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware. It wasn't impossible -- it was impossible, because it was a village in a valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Either you don't know or there wasn't one.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there wasn't one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Goran Djuric known as Talijan?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where his house is?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that even there -- that there was even a gun above his house?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was in the old part, and we were in the upper part, and I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Didn't you just tell us that you were above his house?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't say above his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Didn't you mention that you had been near his house?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was in his house on the 7th of January, and from there I pulled out as I told you before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling me that there was no gun there?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us today that there was nothing suggested that would constitute a military target; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as we were concerned, no, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So how would you describe this gun?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far the village of Vresinje is from Rankovici?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Vresinje is about half an hour away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in kilometres, please?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: It's a half hour walking distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How much is that in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps about two and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was artillery there as well?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else now. Mr. Rankovic, you seem to be a person who is well oriented in time and space.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That means that you are a person giving us reasonable and sensible answers.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are giving us pretty clear answers.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And what I know, I know. And what I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Do you know that all the capacities in the territory of Republika Srpska, which was called at the time the Serbian republic, were utilised for military purposes, including even private property?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please now put on the ELMO document which begins with the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm only going to use a small section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I hope that it is legible, you know, because the copy in English that we are receiving is legible, but the Serbian -- the copy in Serbian is in most page pages --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm only going to use a small portion of this document. And can the page of this document number 00876246 in the B/C/S version be put on the ELMO, as I believe it is legible. And I'm going to quote it, and I ask the witness to look at point 7, because we are only going to focus on it only. Could you please push the paper a little bit up. So page 00876246. And on that page there's item 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the corresponding page in the English version of this document bears ERN number 01900311, and that is page 5 of the said document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness please look at item 7 entitled quartermaster support and the use of the reserves in capacities of the territory. And I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. quote: "In implementing the quartermaster support of units, the basic -- the principal way of providing support would be by relying on the capacity POT and the territory -- that capacity from the territory will be used as follows, to include civilian bakeries, slaughterhouses, warehouses, agriculture farms, agriculture cooperatives, et cetera, commodity reserves of companies, farming estate, agriculture cooperatives and individual farms and that was an order signed by General Djukic of the army of the Republika Srpska. My question is: Jezestica is an agriculture community, and you certainly know that the VRS used the facilities, including the farming estates, agriculture cooperatives, private utilities and -- and capacities.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Jezestica is a farming community. We sow wheat, and we live on farming. We didn't have any factories. You are fully aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Is it true that bakeries, slaughterhouses were used?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have either bakeries or slaughterhouses, not even in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have farmers who could offer produce to the army?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We just produced and grew potatoes, wheat, beans.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had mills?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the army use the mills?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: We used them until the 7th of January. There were five of them. Three were demolished and only one was, in fact, in action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Did the army use those mills?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not the army. We, the local population, used it for our own needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document be given -- be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and that will be Defence Exhibit D33. Again, I please appeal to you to allow a little bit of interval because you're not giving a chance one to the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if it's time for a break now, but this would be a most convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, madam. We will have a 25-minute break starting from now, which basically means we start at ten to one. Ten to one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, while we wait for the accused, the next witness that we have, the next witness that we have, I'm being asked to indicate because this witness is already here. Will you be able to finish with this witness in one day? The next one. You had anticipated two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. The Prosecution will take possibly two hours for direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we should -- I wouldn't imagine that you are going to take four. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a very important witness for us, and I think -- [In English] We are talking about -- [Interpretation] We're talking about Mr. Eric now, Slavisa Eric, as I understood it, and we shall need at least two or two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But -- no. Well, again, we will put our foot down. That witness must finish in one day. So on Tuesday, try and see how you're going to arrange about distributing the time amongst you, and we will need to finish him -- that person in one day. I -- does he have protective measures or -- no. But we'll do our utmost to finish that person. Forgive me when I say him. It might be her, but some names I -- confuse me. I don't know whether they refer to males or to females. This is a male. This is a male.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we'll do our utmost to finish on Tuesday. Okay? Thanks. Yes. Let's try and conclude. You have -- try and finish five minutes before time, please. At least, I mean. Because I have to rush to the airport. At 2.30 I have to be at Schiphol.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will be expeditious.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, you are saying you were not a member of any military unit before August 1992, apart from the village guard.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you, Mr. Rankovic, that today, before this Tribunal, you took -- made a solemn declaration you would speak the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now put on the ELMO document number 013353322, which is document 013353322 and is a part of the document which is the payroll for July 1992 for persons from military post paid for official or troop trips and remuneration. And this is something that was disclosed to us by the Prosecution and is part of the set of documents confiscated from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, please look at number 2124, which is -- has the name Milo Rankovic. And beside the name it says "Platoon commander" who was present from the 1st of June until the 30th of June. That's at the end of the column. Please move the document a little to the left. A little to the left. A bit more. And then in parentheses in the first column next to the name -- or, rather, at the end it says "Milo" where the name Milo Rankovic is, and it seems that the commander received the salaries. But I will ask the witness about that. Mr. Rankovic, is it true that your name is on this list?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is not true. Maybe somebody else signed this, but I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying somebody might have signed this on my behalf, but this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, is it true that you were in company Jezestica 2 where you were a platoon leader?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct, because I was up there in my village, the village of Rankovici. So I couldn't have been a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any other person having the same name and personal details as you, including your father's name, Vaso, in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Can I respond?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you this on another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him answer the question first.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: As you're mentioning my name -- my father's name, I don't recall my father. I have no father. He was killed in 1954.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your father's name while he was alive?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Vaso.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So your father's name was Vaso.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give any explanation why this document should say that you were a platoon leader or commander if you were not?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was not. Maybe somebody had a reason of their own to write this down.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I move on to another document, would you please take a look at this list of names, Jezestica 2. Please move it a little to the right. Yes. Today you mentioned certain people who were killed on the 8th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of August, 1992, there were four civilians among them, the two women who were killed and Milo Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the name under number 2129, this list of Jezestica 2. Is the name of Serbo Djuric there which you mentioned today?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Serbo Djuric?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: It says Djordje. Underneath is Serbo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at number 2134. Andjelko Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: 2135, Dragan Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you turn the page, please. 2195, Milosav Stjepanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned him as well?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were these people combatants?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Stjepanovic Milosav was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Because he was an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why would his name be on this list?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: These are people killed in August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a list for the payroll for July, remuneration or salaries paid for July in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who put a man on that list who was over 70 years of age. I just mentioned those who were killed on the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you trying to say that in your milieu, in your community there were no combatants over the age of 70?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name of Golub Eric mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him, but I'm talking only about my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was a combatant?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't. I can just talk about Milosav Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to tender this document, and I will put a few questions about the attack itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will be Defence Exhibit D34.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today you spoke about this article. There was a lot of testimony about the article you brought. You are familiar with it. Do you need to look at it again?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the newspaper article?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: There's no need.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The subtitle says "Andjelko Mladjenovic also known as Biba was killed defending his village of Jezestica at Bratunac." Does this indicate that this person was a combatant?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: He was, but he was ten metres away from your house. If you can be a combatant in your own house, then he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that these people had no weapons at home?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course we had weapons. I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you fought around your houses on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: We weren't fighting. We were protecting our houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the 8th of August. Did you fight for your houses?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you fired shots near your houses?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: How could they have been shooting when they were killed in front of their house?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what I'm asking you was: Were they killed in the fighting, because it says here Andjelko was killed defending his village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You see the end result of you jumping on him before he's even finished he's even finished his answer -- his answer to your question and he doing exactly the same thing is that the interpretation is suffering and some of the answers he is giving you are not in reply to the questions that you are putting, and I'm sure it's a problem of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just a question of language. The witness was telling that he was defending, and your question, at least in the English translation, you asked for whether he was fighting. Now, do you mean fighting in a different sense than defending? It's only for reasons of clarity. If he was telling about defending, and you asked him -- went on, asking about fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our language and in our area, "defence" implies fighting. Defensive fighting. There is defensive fighting and then there is fighting during an attack. Defensive fighting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Judge Eser is satisfied with the explanation. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for speeding up. I was trying to finish as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, would you please tell us whether it is correct that on the 7th and 10th of April, 2001, you made statements to the Office of the Prosecutor in the police station in Milici and in your house in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I did give a statement in Milici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in your house in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they came from Milici. They followed me, and we went out onto the field. They were from Milici, and they asked me questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On that occasion, you were asked to make a truthful statement about what you personally had seen, and you signed it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the usher to show the witness part of his to show the witness part of his statement given on that occasion on page 02026552. That's the page in the English version. And it's page 03063441 in the Bosnian -- or the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at it, please? Please look at this part of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a specific part from this page that you require the witness to look at? Otherwise, he'll have to read the entire page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will tell you. Explaining the damage to the 54 houses that had been burnt, you said -- can you locate that part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the paragraph which finishes then with the list of the nine persons that were killed. Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found it, Witness? Yes? You said, explaining these 54 houses that had been burnt, you said some had been slightly damaged, some damaged a bit more, and some completely burnt to the ground. This is correct, is it not, Mr. Rankovic?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today, you said something different.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's the old village up there, 54 houses. That was the attack of the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I understood you to say today that all the houses had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. I was speaking of the old houses up there on the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the 8th of August, Mr. Rankovic, and this part of your statement refers to the 8th of August. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And they were all burnt. That was old Jezestica, the old Brdo or hill area. And they were all burnt, except for one which is a new building.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, your statement three years ago was closer in terms of time to the event that you described. Why would you then say something that was not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say anything that was not correct. I can make a list of each household.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will not insist on this point. I will now ask you, Mr. Rankovic, a few questions about the 7th of January, 1993. Talking about this today, you mentioned some people who were killed, and you said that one of them was wearing a military jacket. Would you please tell us who these people who were killed were. Were they civilians or were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: There were some civilians among them, women and elderly men. Among the 19 that were killed on Christmas, there were civilians. There were two women among them, Nevenka and Vida. Then there was also Milo Jokic, an elderly man. Mitar Nikolic was also an elderly man. The others were between 25 or 26 and 50 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Vida Trisic a civilian?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Vida Trisic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly she was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among these people who were killed, how many were combatants?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Combatants? Well, there may have been, what do I know, 13 or 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only 13 or 14?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking about when we were retreating. I can't say we were all there. Some went off to the right. There were only -- there was only us in that house. I'm not talking about all of Jezestica. We weren't all in that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, to the best of your knowledge, among the people killed on that day in Jezestica, how many were combatants?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Fourteen or 15, as far as I know in that house where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, were they at the time fighting with the attackers?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: How could they have been fighting when we were in that house and when we were retreating and fleeing? How could they have been fighting? If they remained behind and fought, those were people who were fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those remained to fight, were they fighting? Were they offering resistance?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not me. I was retreating. I didn't look to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you: Were the combatants there fighting, not were you fighting.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, whether they were shooting or not, I can't say. Everybody -- it was every man for himself. I don't know what the others were doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you about the attackers. Today you described them. Is it true to say that among the attackers there were civilians, women?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Children?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any children, but I did see women.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as we were able to see, 50, 60. I don't know. I couldn't count them. But they were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true to say that these women and civilians you described today took food, livestock, and torched property?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: If they hadn't torched it, it wouldn't have burnt down. I'm sure they took property away. I saw it and so did other people from hilltops.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. It seems, Mr. Rankovic, that these people had come after the 7th of January, 1993, to take possessions from your villages. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say whether they came on that day or ten days later to collect what was left behind. I can't say. The only thing we know, that things were missing from the houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't receive the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat my question because I don't know, Your Honours, if you heard the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We heard the answer, but we did not get the question or what you commented afterwards anyway. I think you ought to repeat the question and he will repeat the answer. I think that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked you, Mr. Rankovic, is it true that those people came after the 7th of January to take possessions from your villages? Could that be true?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I returned on the 23rd, I just found what I found behind my house. So whatever they couldn't take away on that day, they took it away later. They stayed there for about a month.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who these people were? Did you see if those were civilians, army, anyone taking things away?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that it was organised. Whether there were civilians, I would only say that they were all taking things away. I saw them taking my deep freezer and my -- my cooker, and also did my neighbours and my relatives. If I had been there, I would have known more exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Therefore, you did not return to Jezestica until mid-March 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: We only came on the 23rd to collect dead bodies, to see the houses. And there was no place for us to return because everything was burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Rankovic, that there was fighting and that the Serbian forces had been trying to recapture this area and put it back under their control?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: There was no fighting. I don't know, in fact. They just retreated, and I don't know to which positions they withdrew. And that gave us an opportunity to come closer to the houses, because there was a line established about the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me that there was no fighting waged during the winter offensive, a huge winter offensive in January, February, and March 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I will tell you that I left on the 7th or, rather, the 9th of January. I wasn't there, and I cannot tell you anything. I wasn't there, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you know that the Serbian forces had recaptured Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: When we returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that -- that fierce fighting was involved in this recapture?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I was in Serbia until the 23rd of March. So did my wife, because her father was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Rankovic, let us go back now to the photographs of the houses that you identified today.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put on the ELMO the photograph number 01087870. 22 October 2004

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's the photograph which was shown immediately after this memorial plaque on the wall. I said before we saw these photographs. Could you please look at this photograph on the ELMO. Can you see it? Isn't it true, Mr. Rankovic, that this damage could have been inflicted only by heavy artillery weapons? You and I survived the war, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I fully believe that this could be caused by heavy artillery, but I cannot say where and how. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Doesn't this indicate that there was burning or, rather, damage caused by artillery?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to be -- to lie to you or to myself. This was caused by artillery. I came here to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to draw your attention to the house number 01087843. Could we please just correct in the transcript -- it's all right now. Thank you very much. The house beneath. Thank you. Witness, could you please look at the house.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Doesn't this photograph indicate at all any damage caused by fire or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is most certainly the result of burning, because you see that the windows were torn away and all the slabs were ruined. And my house as well as all the other newly built houses suffered the same fate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to which do you draw this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Judging by the wall. Judging by the interior, the basement, 22 October 2004 the -- how could this wooden part be black and the rest of the house white?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What are you are describing I honestly don't see.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I pass by this house on a daily basis. Therefore, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me put to you another question. Mr. Rankovic, do you know who did this?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: It was not us, certainly. No one would set his own house on fire. We took years and worked places in order to be able to build these houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, do you know who did this and when?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: This was done on the 7th of January. And who did this, I don't know their names. I didn't see them. Do you want me to finish?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this with your own eyes that this house was set on fire and who did this?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: We saw with our own eyes that it was burning, but we don't know who set it on fire. It wasn't their neighbours, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether it was a civilian or a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I made a statement that both the civilians and the soldiers and the people dressed in white were involved there, but I don't know who exactly put this house on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I wouldn't dwell on this issue any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will only ask you one more question. At the time when the war was going on in 1992 and early 1993, did you had any knowledge of the command structure of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't finished. No, we didn't. I only knew that we were attacked, that our neighbours from those villages attacked, but who commanded them, whether it was Huso or Haso, or anyone else, I never saw them and I cannot say. I cannot put the blame on anyone because I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That means that you -- you had been attacked by your neighbours from the local surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from those directions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Is there -- my apologies to the interpreters for not switching on the mike. Is there a re-examination, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, just quickly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please go through it as quickly as you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Rankovic, you just testified that when you were asked about the attacks from the neighbouring villages, do you know whether the neighbours in those neighbouring villages attacked your village, or did they come from that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: They came from that direction. So logically if the attack came on to Rankovici, perhaps it could have come from Cizmici and any other direction. I don't know. That was an all-out attack on the village. So it came from the sides where these villages are situated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And these are Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, Defence counsel inquired whether or not soldiers and combatants had been killed in the attack on 7 January 1993. Could you tell us, the individuals who died as a result of that attack on your village, were they members of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: They were members of the village guard. For example, in Rankovici or Djurici and Kijevici, a smaller number of them were killed on Christmas, but we sustained a heavier attack. And this is the left side, and that is where the majority of the fatalities took place, because families were closer knit together, and the families in Djermani and the other hamlet suffers less.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So were they members of the VRS or were they members of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the village guard. As I said, we had the uniforms we had been issued long before the war. We put them on what we had, just as they did. Some of them wore civilian clothes, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just answer the question. Don't tell us a whole story.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And respect to the women you saw during the attack, did the women come at the same time the village was attacked initially, or did they come later? The women you observed taking items away from the village.

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: They came later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it, finished.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They came later after their army or combatants, or call it what you will. They first took things away, and then the women followed, took oxen-driven carts and took away the remaining possessions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Rankovic, you still have a few minutes to bear with us. Judge Brydensholt would like to put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: You mentioned that you had uniforms which all of your -- your other citizens in your village also had, and you mentioned that the Muslims as well had some sort of uniforms which they have had for many years, I understand. Among the uniforms you had from your time serving in the army, was there any white uniform for winter combat or was that a new thing you saw in January?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, we saw just a few white uniforms. They were not exactly military, and there were some civilians. So there were just a few, about ten or a dozen of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: But could that white uniform, or what you call it, be something the persons have got from the army when they were demobilised, when they have served their time in the army, or was it their private -- what kind of clothes was it?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: We who served the army earlier had the same uniforms. Then you had civilians. And as for these, I wouldn't know whether they were army personnel or not. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The question I had had is already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I see. All right. Okay. I just want this because the question Judge Brydensholt put to you is very important. Basically you and your other villagers that had, as you explained to us, in your household uniforms that you use once every two years, amongst those uniforms did you also have white uniforms? You and your colleagues in the village and in the area where you lived. For example, if on the 7th of January you decided to wear a white uniform, would you have found one in your house or not?

utterances.speaker: MILO RANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't have those white uniforms. As I said, during the attack by our neighbours, I saw that some ten or 15 of them were wearing white, but we didn't have such uniforms. And basically the previous army never had this kind of uniform before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So, Mr. Rankovic, on behalf of Judge Brydensholt who comes from Denmark and Judge Eser who comes from Germany and myself, my name is Carmel Agius, and I come from the island of Malta, and on behalf of the Trial Chamber and also of the Tribunal I would like to thank you for having come over here to The Hague to give evidence in this trial against Naser Oric. You will be escorted now by Madam Usher, and you will be given all the attention and assistance you require in order to facilitate your return back home. On behalf of everyone in this courtroom, I would like to wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think we can call it a day. We will resume on Tuesday, please, God. And the next witness you, you know where he is, and we will all be endeavouring to finish with that witness on Tuesday. Have a nice weekend, a long weekend this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of October, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.40 p.m.,
